# CP cavities give a volume-free local-fault expansion for centered HP noise
30 October 2026. New working construction; independent review pending. This is a finite scheduled-circuit noise-interface theorem, not a new universal fault-tolerance theorem or a claim of historical novelty.

## 1. Exact input contract
Let S be finitely many bounded-dimensional system sites, with an arbitrary retained finite-dimensional bath B. Intended gates form a fixed finite schedule. At any time their active supports are disjoint blocks, each of at most g sites; include idle blocks as locations. Each location lasts at most tau. Its intended time-local generator is a CPTP generator acting only on that block. Instantaneous intended CPTP gates at the partition boundaries can also be inserted. Adaptive scheduling is not silently included.

The actual time-local generator is

 L(t)=L_id(t)+L_B,raw(t)+sum_e N_e(t).

The complete generator produces CPTP propagators on every time interval. Each N_e is centered (trace-annihilating), Hermiticity-preserving, and acts on at most q system sites and the bath. It need NOT generate CP dynamics on its own. Its completely bounded trace norm is at most eta_e(t), with incident bound sum_(e contains i) eta_e(t)<=eta for every system site. The raw bath generator need not be CP separately. Finite-dimensional bounded piecewise-continuous coefficients suffice below. Infinite bath extensions require the corresponding bounded-normal generator/dilation/limit hypotheses and are not asserted here.

All norms below are complete trace norms, and every estimate is uniform over the initial bath state, system-bath correlations, and retained references. No positive fault trajectory is assumed.

# Exact fault-class support and a finite gadget receiving rule
30 October 2026. Companion derivation for CP_CAVITY_LOCAL_FAULT_BRIDGE.md; no universal threshold or autonomous compiler claim.

## 1. Why bath-only cavity changes do not spoil location support
A fault class F means the linear span of circuit maps in which every location outside F is its ideal gate, while locations in F may undergo arbitrary system/bath maps. Arbitrary bath-only evolution is allowed between locations. This is the nonprobabilistic, shared-bath fault-class meaning, not a distribution of independent CPTP errors.

On a synchronized layer of disjoint gate blocks, a cavity generator has the form

 sum_(j in R)L_id,j + Id_R tensor K_complement,

where K_complement is an actual CPTP generator. The two pieces commute on system supports. The layer propagator is therefore exactly the tensor product of the intended maps on R and an arbitrary joint map on the other active blocks and bath. A finite system matrix-unit expansion of the latter expresses it as a linear combination of products of maps on those other blocks, with bath-map coefficients. Each coefficient can be attached to one allowed faulty location, with bath-only history allowed when none is present. No norm estimate is taken on this expansion; its purpose is ONLY to establish linear-span support.

Composition over layers proves that T^R lies in the fault class Lambda without R. Each summand of E_F has R containing Lambda without F. The fault classes are nested, so E_F lies in class F. In particular E_empty is the ideal system circuit tensored with a bath channel, even though that bath channel differs from the bath dynamics of other cavities. It preserves the intended system/reference operation, including for initially correlated system-bath inputs.

For fixed schedules resolved into smaller intervals, apply the same argument on each interval where the active block partition is fixed. The resulting class allows arbitrary interactions inside each declared faulty location's duration; no interaction on an ideal location remains. A threshold proof formulated for strictly layered gate boxes can instead use the explicitly layered version, with any refinement overhead counted. Do not claim an arbitrary overlapping autonomous generator is a scheduled disjoint-gate circuit.

30 October 2026. The frozen sources and their exact hashes are in sources/ and SOURCE_SHA256.txt. This review was performed separately from the construction. It does not assess historical novelty.

## Verdict

**PASS for the stated finite, bounded, fixed-schedule, joint-CP-divisible circuit noise-interface theorem, and for the exact disjoint-gadget sieve under its separately supplied correctness premise.** No load-bearing counterexample was found. The inclusive signed fault bound is

 ||sum_(F contains S0) E_F||_diamond <= [2*3^(q-1)*g*eta*tau]^(|S0|/q),

when the bracket is at most one. There is no device-volume or total-runtime exponential in this bound. The complete generator must generate CPTP propagators on EVERY interval; a merely CPTP final channel or a non-CP-divisible reduced generator is insufficient. The finite-dimensional bounded assumptions are substantive.

This is not a complete new fault-tolerance threshold theorem. Actual good-gadget correctness, overlapping extended-rectangle bookkeeping where used, input preparation, physical gates, detectors, and decoder/encoding resources remain separate. Nor is this a native autonomous controller construction. The primary Hamiltonian common-bath threshold results cited by the author remain established prior machinery.

## 1. The cavity really is a legitimate generator

For an active selected block R, let E_R insert its normalized maximally mixed state and let R_R denote partial trace. Both maps are CPTP. Therefore A->R_R A E_R is contractive in complete trace norm. Tensoring the identity on the selected block preserves the diamond norm, so the generator projection P_R has norm at most one. On disjoint active blocks, normalized embeddings and partial traces commute; consequently the P_j commute and P_R=product P_j. Idempotence follows directly.

If L is the actual joint generator, the reduced map R_R exp(hL) E_R is CPTP, is the identity at h=0, and has derivative R_R L E_R. In finite dimensions, the product limit of these short-step maps proves that this derivative is a CPTP generator. This does not require a subsystem of the original noise decomposition to generate a positive evolution.
